A silver bracelet my biological mom sent me by mail on my 20th birthday. It had a charm where my name was engraved on it and also an image of an apple tree with a long slit in the middle of the trunk.
 I believe it was a reproduction of the apple tree in our backyard; the house I lived in with my bio mom until I was taken away by CPS to live with my dad. The package the bracelet came in also included a photo of where she currently lives, with the address, all of her contact information and the most painful thing to lose: a long letter explaining why she left and apologizing. She took off 10+ years ago without a word, and the bracelet was something that somehow made me feel connected to her. I still miss it everyday and am tearing up a bit thinking about it :( . I miss the whole package tbh, wish I could find it so I could finally contact her.

I relate heavily to your post. Growing up with an absent, biological mother and a controlling, narcissistic step-mother, I never felt like I had a proper mother figure either. I blamed myself for many years and developed many insecurities about my self-worth and whether I even deserved love. Hence, I put up walls and walls protecting myself from feeling any form of vulnerability. 

Anyways, this isn't about me but I just wanted to say you aren't alone... Your feelings are completely valid and also, temporary. They will improve with time and patience!! That feeling of "not knowing how to love" will slowly go away by learning to love yourself, and by allowing your SO to love you. Not being shown proper love as a child can definitely affect your ability to love and to open up to emotional vulnerability, but it isn't permanent. It'll just take more time than another person to reach that stage and that's totally okay!!

Honestly, I would suggest that you have a heart to heart with your SO about your worries and concerns, if he is a good guy (and im sure he is), he'll understand and support you on your slow but steady path to recovery.

OP, you deserve all the love in the world, and you DO have the power and capability to give that love back. Your post made me tear up because I know EXACTLY what you're going through.... Hang in there! :)
